utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-68-T, the Prosecutor versus Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam and good afternoon to you. Mr. Oric, can you follow the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours, ladies and gentlemen. I can follow the proceeding in my mother tongue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. Please sit down. Appearances for -- and good afternoon to you, appearances for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you as well, Your Honours. My name is Jan Wubben, lead counsel for the Prosecution. So good afternoon to my learned friends of the Defence. I'm here together with co-counsel, Mr. Gramsci Di Fazio, and our case manager, Ms. Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Wubben and good afternoon to you and your team. Appearances for Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, Vasvija Vidovic and John Jones appearing on behalf of Mr. Naser Oric. Today with us are our legal assistant, Ms. Adisa Mehic, and our CaseMap manager, Mr. Geoff Roberts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Vidovic and good afternoon to you and your team. Are there any preliminaries before we start with the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I understood you well, yesterday, although it wasn't you, Mr. Wubben, it was Ms. Sellers, you are renouncing to witness number 51 Rajko Sarenac.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That's right, Your Honour, we will not call that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So when will you finish?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: That means that we aim to finish on the 31st of May. That's the Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Doesn't change anything, in other words?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's the important thing because I wanted to make sure that no one is caught on the wrong foot, and that includes our staff as well. But that's okay. That's fine. That's fine, and I appreciate your cooperation, Mr. Wubben. I take it that you will be leading this -- all right. Let's bring the witness in, please. I also take it that you will conclude today? MR. DI FAZIO: No question about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And that you will have the entire of Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: That should be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: I may even be finished before the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's even better. I mean, that's the only good news I would have received today, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And welcome to this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I take it that you are receiving interpretation in your own language. If at any time in the course of your testimony today and Monday you have difficulties in receiving interpretation, please draw our attention straight away and we will rectify that. That applies also if the sound level is not to your liking. You are about to start giving evidence as a witness brought forward by the Prosecution and our Rules require that before you do so, you enter a solemn declaration equivalent to an oath in the sense that in the course of your testimony, you will be speaking the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text is contained in a piece of paper that Mr. Usher is going to hand to you now. Please read it out aloud and that will be your solemn undertaking with us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Delic. Please make yourself comfortable. Now, let me introduce to you the Bench. I am the Presiding Judge, my name is Carmel Agius and I come from Malta. To my right I have Judge Hans Hendrik Brydensholt from Denmark. To my left I have Judge Albin Eser from Germany. Together we are presiding over this trial that has been going on for a few months against Naser Oric. To your right you have the team from -- for the Prosecution, amongst which the nearest person to you is Mr. Di Fazio who will be examining you in chief. To your left you have the team for the Defence led by Madam Vidovic but the cross-examination will be conducted by Mr. Jones who is co-counsel with Madam Vidovic in the defence of Mr. Oric. Yes. I would last but not least before I hand you over to Mr. Di Fazio, I would suggest to you that you try to answer the questions as precisely as possible to the best of your ability, but also as concisely as possible. In other words, please try to answer the question, the whole question and nothing but the question. Don't try to give us more information than you are being asked to give. Do I make myself clear to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Completely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Di Fazio, he's in your hands. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honour. Examined by Mr. Di Fazio: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Delic, I'd like you to confirm for me, if you may, these particular details, and I could I ask, Mr. Usher if we could move the ELMO machine because I can't see the face of the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, by all means, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thanks very much. I appreciate that. All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Personal background and details. Tell me if these are correct and correct anything you want to. You're a Bosniak, you were born in September of 1954, you were born in Gorazde in Bosnia and Herzegovina. As far as your educational background is concerned, in 1973 you completed your secondary schooling. In 1977, you completed your JNA military academy training. In 1991, you completed your ground forces Command Staff academy training, and furthermore, you have obtained a masters degree in political science which you obtained in 2000. Those details correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did you -- where did you obtain your masters degree in political science?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I obtained my masters degree in political science in Sarajevo --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: -- with the law of political science -- with the school of political science.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Your military appointments in the former JNA included these positions: You were at some stage assistant to the Chief of Staff for operational and educational issues; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: For a short while, during 1991.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And where was that position located?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The position was with the Varazdin Corps after I finished the education on the ground forces, and during -- that was a part of the Varazdin Corps of the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You were an intelligence officer with the 17th Corps of the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Upon my return from Varazdin that is from the Republic of Croatia I was transferred to the Tuzla Corps and I was the intelligence secretary with the 5th Corps of the JNA in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction with the 17th Corps in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was until March 1992 and I only worked part time, four hours a day. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In April of 1992, you left the JNA, and at some point between the 18th and the 22nd of April 1992, you were appointed commander of the Municipal Territorial Defence Staff in Tuzla; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 10th of November, 1992, you were appointed commander of the 5th or 5 Operational Group in Tuzla. Can you confirm that or correct me?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In November of 1994, you were appointed commander of the 2nd Corps of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Tuzla; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You remained in the army until -- in the ABiH army, until October of 2000, but from 1997 until 2001, you also were a professor at the University of Tuzla. Those two --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on the 5th of October 2002, you were elected as a deputy in the House of Representatives in the parliament of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and you remain to this day a member of parliament; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Throughout the greater part of the period of time between 1992 -- April of 1992 and 1995, regardless of whatever command positions you held, were you in the main located in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the entire war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber when you first met, and I mean personally, face to face, with Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I met Brigadier Naser Oric for the first time once he returned from Srebrenica in 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that just prior to the fall of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps two months prior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll return to that later. In the course of your duties in the army, and in particular in the course of your duties between April of 1992 and 1995, did you become familiar with the -- the documentation used by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. To the extent of the amount of information that would reach me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, of course. And in giving evidence today, I'd like you at all times, if you can, to inform the Trial Chamber when you're asserting something as a result of your own direct knowledge and when you're asserting something on the basis of what you have heard or been told. I'd like to show you a series of documents now. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit P279? Yes, it's on Sanction, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: The first question --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first question that I wish to ask you is this: Have you ever seen this document before? Are you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did see this order previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that when you were stationed in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: One could say that that was so because as a commander, I did not receive this order, but I did see -- I was given this order after the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you in fact laid eyes on it after the cessation of hostilities and not in August of 1992 when it was apparently created; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. Having taken over the duty of the corps commander, I did not go through the archives in order to locate such documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall the circumstances under which you saw it after the cessation of hostilities? How was it that you came to see it, become aware of it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I was personally engaged as military expert in the case of the late General Alagic. Hence a part of the documentation pertaining to the initial periods of aggression against the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was accessible to me. Based on that, I was given an opportunity to see this document as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The part of the document that I want to take you to is contained in paragraphs 1 and 2. The following corps are formed in the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, then lists a number of army corps. The first one is based in Sarajevo, the second one in Tuzla. You see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. In paragraph 2, it asserts that the zones of responsibility of these corps that I've just directed your attention to cover the territories of the following municipalities. And in particular the 2nd corps the headquarters of which is in Tuzla covered various municipalities, one of which is Srebrenica. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is precisely so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber if armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina that operated in Srebrenica were therefore subordinated to the headquarters of the 2nd Corps located in Tuzla? Is that a correct understanding of the document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: That would be the logical interpretation, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. However, a number of these municipalities, were they at the time that this document was created, in August of 1992, and in the period of time immediately preceding August of 1992, and after August of 1992 up until 1995, were some of those municipalities under Serb forces, under the control of Serb military forces?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, almost half of these municipalities were not under the control of the regular armed forces and authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and I will list them. Bijeljina, Bosanski Brod, Bosanski Samac, the largest portion of Bratunac, Derventa, Doboj, and the municipalities of Kalesija, Lopare, in full, Modrica, in fall, a part of the Odzak municipality, and a part of the Srebrenica municipality, Teslic, Sekovici, Ugljevik, Vlasenica, almost the entire territory of Zvornik. In those municipalities, there were no units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and they were not under the control of the civilian authorities of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with that document. And perhaps if I can save Mr. Usher a trip I'd also like to produce P76 to the witness. General Delic, you've seen this document in the last two days of proofing here. Up until you came to The Hague, had you ever laid eyes on this document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Until my arrival to The Hague, I have never seen such a document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know or can you tell us if the appointment of Mr. Oric as commander of the Srebrenica municipality TO, pursuant to Article 18, paragraph 1, item 1 of the decree law, is apparently - I'm only talking about the face of the document - apparently done in accordance with the correct legislation? If you don't know, please say so.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I personally think that it is rather extraordinary to appoint a commander using two very short sentences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you normally have expected --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. MR. DI FAZIO: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you normally have expected this sort of appointment to be a -- contained in a more voluble document, a longer document?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, but in 1992, everything was possible, including this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, before you finish with that document. Could he possibly recognise the signature on that document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the signature is unclear. I cannot say with certainty what it is, and I cannot see it from the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Perhaps just one other question, sorry, that arises from His Honour's question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The document appears to emanate from the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina TO Staff, Sarajevo. Is that where one would normally expect such an appointment to emanate from? This type of appointment to -- as commander of the Srebrenica TO?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Under the regulation, the TO Staff commanders in municipalities were appointed by this particular organ, that is the Republican Staff of the TO.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P129.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, this is a document that has been shown to you in the last two days since your arrival in The Hague. Just look at it, acquaint yourself with it.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is all right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber if you saw this document during the course of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I did not see this document during the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, but I implemented a part of it pertaining to the municipality of Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Did you see an order in similar or identical terms directed to you in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, an excerpt of the order was sent to me personally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you just tell the Trial Chamber why you did not see the full order, if you only saw an excerpt?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Within the military system of command and control and the military hierarchy, it is not regular practice that the command at the third level communicates directly with the first instance command. I had to communicate via the corps command. As you see in the document, this was received by the District Defence Staff or later it was the 2nd Corps of the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The order requires certain organisational changes to be conducted. If you flick through the document - Your Honours will find it at page 5, the relevant part - it purports to effect -- or issue orders to ABiH armed forces in Srebrenica municipality. There is just a few things that I would like you to explain to the Trial Chamber as best you can because it's not entirely clear in English. Paragraph A, can you read paragraph A, please? Can you tell the Trial Chamber what, in effect, that order is seeking?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, under item 9, with the title, in the Srebrenica municipality, under subparagraph A, it states the following: "The Municipal Defence Staff and headquarters support units, numerical designation T-30072, duration of mobilisation, 12 hours." From my point of view, that would mean that this particular municipal staff, as of the moment of the issuing of the order, that that particular staff had to be mobilised within 12 hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you -- you don't have to read them out individually. We can save time if you don't do that, but can you take us through each of the subheadings, B, C, D, and explain in more straightforward terms the actual, practical effect of these orders to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Under B, the following is defined. Detachments of the armed forces as follows, this is first and the second detachment with numerical designations T-30360 and T-30361. Under C, independent infantry companies of the armed forces, according to the war formation for an independent infantry company of the TO; and item D, independent platoons according to war deployment or war formation for an independent rifle platoon of the TO, number T-412108. Paragraph ends with war units cited under A and B are to be set up according to the aforementioned organisational order. The coordinator of the mobilisation plan for all war units cited in this item shall be the Srebrenica Municipal Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell the Trial Chamber that you received an order in accordance with the -- directed to you in Tuzla, in accordance or emanating from this general order?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if a similar order based on this general order was delivered to ABiH armed forces in the Srebrenica municipality? Do you know? If you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: As concerns the municipality of Srebrenica, I have no knowledge about that, but as for the municipality of Tuzla, the units that were formed before that were later on verified.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you can't say if a similar order, similar to the one you received in Tuzla, was or was not sent to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've finished with that document. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown Exhibit P201.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please look at this document, reacquaint yourself with it? It was shown to you here. First question I want to ask you is -- it's apparently signed by Zeljko Knez. Does that signature -- do you recognise that signature?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do recognise the signature of my commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you become familiar with that signature during the course of carrying out your duties in the years 1992 to 1995?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I had opportunities to meet Mr. Zeljko Knez even before the combat operations because in the JNA he had been my battalion commander for two years, at the time when I was the commander of an infantry company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But I'm actually more interested -- thank you for informing us that you know him, but I'm actually more interested in the signature. Look at the signature. First question: Did you ever become familiar through your contacts and your work with him, did you become familiar with his signature? And secondly, is that his signature, if you did become familiar?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Although it's unclear, I'm certain it's his signature. The copy is blurred but I'm sure it's his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The actual text of the order we can deal with fairly quickly. It's an order establishing training centres in various locations, including Tuzla and Srebrenica, as you can see under paragraph 1. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you, in fact, establish a training centre in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: It existed in Tuzla throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Thanks, but did you set one up pursuant to, in response to, this order?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely, pursuant to this order. The same order, without this sign that says Srebrenica, is one that I received as commander of the Tuzla TO staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it the case -- well, let me withdraw that, rephrase it. Can you tell us if you know, and only if you know, whether a similar training centre was ever set up in Srebrenica or not? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No. In the period from 1992 until the end of 1994, I do not know what happened in Srebrenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like you to look at the top right-hand corner of the original there, the B/C/S version. You have in handwriting the word "Srebrenica." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber the circumstances under which that hand -- that sort of handwriting entry would be made on the document such as this, the stage at which it would be placed on a document such as this? In other words, take the Trial Chamber, just listen to my question. Take the Trial Chamber through the process from the point at which the order is made, its creation on writing, its placing on paper, to the points where such a handwritten entry might be made, thank you.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in the commands where I commanded and where I was present during the war and before the war, there were regulations on the administrative proceedings of these units. These regulations clearly defined the manner in which documentation circulated within military units. There was only one original document, and all other copies were made in the numbers required, depending on how many people needed to use them. They were registered in the office. They were given numbers in sequence and then sent to their immediate users. In every organisational and establishment structure, there had to be a register from which you could see where and when which document was sent and possibly who received it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. But how does the handwriting fit in with the answer that you have just provided us? Does the appearance of the handwriting on this particular document mean that it is the one original document that you spoke of, or is it one of the other copies that were made of the original? That's the first point that I want to know.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Without going into the content of this document, there is only one original which remains in the archives of the unit. The other copies are copied in the office, distributing the document, and then in the office they would write on each copy to whom it was to be delivered. Looking at this, the office of the district Territorial Defence staff intended to send this document to the Municipal Staff of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence. That's how I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Okay. So someone writes in Srebrenica on the document intended to go to Srebrenica. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No. I don't think we understand one another. The original document is copied, but without what it says here in handwriting, Srebrenica, without mentioning to whom it is being sent. And then on the copies, they add -- they write in to whom the documents were to be sent, and then they sent these documents on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. That's right. So the appearance of the word "Srebrenica" in handwriting, does that indicate to you that this particular document with that writing was intended to be sent, physically sent, to Srebrenica? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. You're right. This is the only conclusion I can draw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, whether it was actually sent or not, do you have any knowledge about that? And I'm asking about this particular document.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: You could check this information only through the deliveries book in the command of the Tuzla Territorial Defence staff. I can only speculate but I'm not here to speculate, only to tell you what I know and what is the truth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If it wasn't sent to Tuzla -- to Srebrenica, would you expect to find the original plus this copy with the handwritten words -- hand written word, "Srebrenica", only in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: That's what I would expect to happen, yes, only in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, because you are presenting it to the witness and he is taking it for granted that it is so and it can only be so. But I can figure out, for example, that if it could not be delivered in the normal manner, it could also be faxed, and if it is faxed, the original will remain in Tuzla but the faxed copy would have reached Srebrenica. So there is that option also. In other words, the fact that the original, this document, with the written, handwritten name "Srebrenica," is found in Tuzla, does not necessarily mean that it has never reached Srebrenica. It could have been faxed. MR. DI FAZIO: I know that. If Your Honours please, and at some stage later in the Prosecution submission you'll be reminded of the evidence of Rasim Manas and where the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, because the witness is here. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Particularly on that point the witness himself has said that he's not here to speculate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: -- and that these are very involved questions which are inviting him to do precisely that. These are submissions which can be made in the due course of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. The fact is, it's wrong to draw the conclusion or to suggest to the witness the conclusion that the fact that this may have been traced or found in Tuzla means that it never reached Srebrenica. MR. DI FAZIO: That's not my point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then make it clear. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm trying to do precisely the opposite to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then make it clear to the witness. And while we are at it, perhaps while the witness has the document right in front of him, right above those -- that name, the "Srebrenica," the handwritten name of the town, in the middle of the top part of the page, there is what looks like a signature. Does that look familiar to him? Can he identify that signature? MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You heard His Honour's question. Can you -- can you inform us or shed any light on that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may comment. What Your Honour said is precisely so. As for this signature, I don't know whose it is. It may be somebody who compiled the original document. In my career, my practice was that all those who wrote an order and brought it to me for my signature should sign the original as well before I signed it so that if something went wrong, these signatures would be there. However, as for this document, I do not know why this signature is there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... was shown on computer evidence for sure. I want to make sure that the public who may have been following the proceedings has the opportunity of seeing this document on the ELMO. So put it briefly, the original, the B/C/S version on the ELMO, please. And could you also zoom on the top part of the first page? The top part of the first page, so that the public can see what the witness was being referred to, that is the written name of Srebrenica, handwritten name of Srebrenica, plus that unidentified signature in the middle of the top of the page, and then let's put on the ELMO the second page, lower half, please, where there is the signature of the commandant Zeljko Knez which has been recognised for all intents and purposes although it's not that clear, by the witness. All right? Okay. You can remove the two documents, the two pages, and we can proceed with your questions, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just one more question, not necessarily for -- I don't need the document. But just arising from His Honour's -- what His Honour said, do you know if there were any fax facilities in existence at around the time of July 1992 as between Tuzla and Srebrenica? And again, that constant reminder, if you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I've finished with the document, if Your Honours please. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness be shown P143.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, there is no secret that you have seen this document, at least in the last couple of days here in The Hague. My first question is, look at the signature at the back of the document. Do you recognise it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the signature of the commander of the district staff, Mr. Zeljko Knez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Acquaint yourself with the content of the order and tell the Trial Chamber if you're aware of any such order having been issued during --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Take it as a rule that although we have access to the -- to Sanction and we can follow, the public is not in a position to follow -- are they in a position to follow Sanction as well? If it's -- oh, I see. All right. Okay. MR. DI FAZIO: Apparently it's broadcast, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't know. I mean, because I -- I'm seeing what I need to follow here on my screen and I can't see what the public has access to. So I want to make sure that the public, as well as the accused, can see the document. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So -- thank you, Witness. The signature at the back of the document, is it -- no.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: It's the same as the previous signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me rephrase my question. Look at the content of the document and tell the Trial Chamber if you're aware of any such order having been issued around October 1992.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I received the identical order as the commander of the TO Staff of the Tuzla Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you carry out the order in accordance with the terms --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to this order, in the Municipal Staff of the Tuzla Territorial Defence, the situation that was already in place was simply approved. I only acted on what was not in the -- in compliance with this, in the previous establishment structure.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd just like to be absolutely clear. Are you saying that there was -- you had already formed military police structures prior to this order having been issued and that the structures you had set up complied with this order in any event?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Precisely so, Mr. Di Fazio. You see that there is no mention here of the Tuzla Municipal Staff. I was duty bound to carry out only the second part of the order which says that the company should have 105 men and about the moral profile of those entering the military police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could you look at paragraph 2 of the order? That says that the chiefs of security in Municipal Defence Staffs, such as Tuzla or Srebrenica or wherever, have to control the units of the military police in professional terms. Can -- it's not entirely clear in the English translation. Can you just explain that in a little more detail to the Trial Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, item 2 regulates the method of command and control of the military police organs. It says here that the chiefs of security in municipal defence staffs or brigades shall control the units of military police in professional terms. This is horizontal control. As for the control of the work and the carrying out of the assignments, this shall be done by the chief of security of the Tuzla District Defence Staff or a person he appoints, as it says here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber if the effect of this order was that military police and the security organs in Municipal Defence Staffs were therefore subordinated to the chiefs? Sorry, the commanders of those municipal defence staffs?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: It says "chiefs of security," it didn't say commanders. That's misreading. MR. DI FAZIO: Chiefs of security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were they subordinated to the Municipal Defence Staffs?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The chiefs of security within the Territorial Defence Staffs were subordinate to the commander of the Territorial Defence Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did that change at all in the period of April 1995 until the end of the war? Until 1995, at least?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: This relationship between the security organ and the commander did not change until the end of the war. There was a horizontal and vertical hierarchy. The vertical relationship was that of superior and subordinate, which meant that the chief of security was subordinate to the staff commander. Horizontally he could cooperate both with the subordinate chiefs and those from the higher command, both the lower and the higher commands. Professionally, they carried out tasks with that organ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps he can enlighten us on this because we are really interested in what was the position in 1992, in particular, and 1993, early parts of 1993. This document is dated 14th of October of 1992. What was the position before the 14th of October 1992? And after the war had started. I mean between April, in other words, and October, 1992, when this document is issued.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the system was not well organised and attempts were being made to organise it properly to bring it into line with the kind of system that exists in every army everywhere.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It may not have been organised properly but can you tell us if in the period preceding the 14th of October 1992, whether military police and the security organ were subordinated to local TO commanders?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm bearing in mind the answer which the witness gave earlier which was, I'm quoting, "in the period from 1992 until the end of 1994, I do not know what happened in Srebrenica municipality." If his question is confined to what happened in Tuzla, then that's fair enough. If it's a question about Srebrenica, then we need to be clear because so far the witness has said he didn't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, you're perfectly right. Mr. Di Fazio, you are of course free to pose the question, but keep in mind also what the witness has already stated in regard to Srebrenica, and if you want to articulate it further, you have of course all the possibility to do so. MR. DI FAZIO: Grateful to Mr. Jones for reminding me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. And I think it's very important, the point he has raised. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, yes, quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What was the position in -- MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about Srebrenica. You've already told us you don't know. I'm asking you about the situation prior to October of 1992 -- I'm asking you about the situation in Tuzla and if you know what the situation was in other areas of the country, other than Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand your question, Mr. Di Fazio. In no municipality in the free territory of the then Tuzla canton, and district, this is a civilian term, the conditions were not the same. Even neighbouring municipalities to Tuzla did not have the same material and human resources which would enable them to organise themselves in the way demanded by military organisation and practice. Specifically in Tuzla municipality, as for what we were able to do, we attempted to set up the system as soon as possible, and we were in the vanguard, in the forefront, of everything that was happening in this respect, compared to the District Staff which had its headquarters in Tuzla. If it's of assistance, I think in most neighbouring municipalities, this order was complied with for the most part. I am convinced that, at least where the municipalities of Tuzla are concerned, these units of the military police were established.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but as you know, I'm asking you about the situation that applied prior to October of 1992. Now, you've already commented and told us the effect of this order, vis-a-vis subordination, military police, and the security organ, post disorder. Now, prior to this order. Remember, don't comment on Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: If you are seeking my comment, an order comes from the situation in the field or rather a problem in the field. I formed the military police company and I had it complete by June 1992. But the problems were inside the army, within the command and control system, as well as the problems of relationship between municipal and district staffs. The district Staff was in its inception. It did not have its logistic services and no impact on municipal staffs, and the most important role of that staff was to be active in the field. That's why this order, in order to regulate their relationship, amongst other things to improve the security situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a correction for the transcript. The witness stated that the Municipal Staff was in its inception. The record reflects the District Staff, which is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the Municipal Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic, and thank you, Mr. Delic. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, I've finished with that document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Avoid documents for a few moments. You've told us that you met Mr. Oric for the first time in 1995 at some point prior to the fall of Srebrenica. During the course of 1992 and 1993, did you come to know of Mr. Oric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did come to know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were your sources of information at that time?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: As with other citizens, one of my sources of information were the media, the radio and the TV. The second source of information were the meetings of the Territorial Staff of the TO in Tuzla, and I attended such meetings, and on one occasion the subject of discussion was Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's break that up a bit. First of all we will come to the meetings later but first let's look at the media. What newspapers or what TV did you read or hear in which -- where Mr. Oric was introduced to you, as a person, as a character?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I didn't have much time on our hands to read or to watch TV, but I believe that was the radio television channel of the Tuzla canton, as it exists even today, and it included ham radio operators reporting on events, and radio-television Tuzla also mentioned the issue. But I also believe a magazine called Armija Ljiljana wrote about that at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Armija -- I won't even attempt the second word, I apologise. This magazine, is that an army magazine, a BiH army magazine or newspaper?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is a magazine that wrote about events on frontlines and important events from individual units and corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. How was Mr. Oric described in these media sources?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: As regards those media reports, my impression of Brigadier Naser Oric was that of a courageous man who commanded that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The wider area of Srebrenica, where he was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you see such commentary in Armija Ljiljana -- let me finish the question actually, namely that he was courageous, secondly that he was the commander in that area?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly whether I read it in Armija Ljiljana, but I still maintain that I did hear what I just said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also mentioned earlier that another source of information that you had about Mr. Oric prior to your meeting him was meetings that you attended. It's not in dispute that in -- MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just bear with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not in dispute that there was -- Srebrenica was demilitarised in the first quarter of 1993. I'm sorry I can't recall the precise date. In relation to that --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: On the 8th of May 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thanks. Prior to that date, did you attend any such meetings to discuss the situation in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Precisely so. One of the meetings was called in the command of the then corps of the 2nd Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the subject of discussion was aid to the populace of Srebrenica and deploying a unit to Srebrenica, and the unit was supposed to be organised by the 2nd Corps of the ABiH. The meeting was attended by the commanders of municipal staffs in order to receive specific tasks, first and foremost, concerning material and equipment, that had to issue the unit with. The unit had to be manned from the people from Podrinje, and sent to combat some 100 kilometres away from Tuzla to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this meeting also concerned with the issue of organising, actually bringing about, this -- this result, getting aid into Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, precisely so. A brigade was supposed to be formed in order to help the people on Srebrenica to survive there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you said that the meeting was called in the command of the corps of the 2nd Corps of the ABiH army. Can you tell the Trial Chamber the highest ranking military officers who attended this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I'm certain that all Municipal TO Staff commanders around Tuzla were present, as well as the immediate corps command. I can list the people, or rather the regions, Tuzla, Lukavac, Zivinice, Srebrenik, Kalesija, Gradacac, the free territories of Brcko, Gracanica, the free territories of Doboj East. That is what comprised the single free territory under the then authorities. It was called the Tuzla District. Today it is known under the name of Tuzla Canton.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was the single most -- who was the single most high-ranking officer?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The highest ranking officer was the corps commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was his name?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was the end of 1992 or the beginning of 1993. I cannot recall, but I believe it could have been only Zeljko Knez or Hazim Cavic, both generals.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, to effect -- carry out a mission like that, get aid into Srebrenica, military aid, and civilian aid, would have involved - you correct me if I'm wrong - a dangerous mission through enemy territory and penetration into the area of the Srebrenica enclave with -- held by ABiH forces. Am I correct or not in that description?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was a very risky operation. One had to go through 100 kilometres of the enemy's territory in order to reach Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber if it was important to you, attending that meeting, and to the other military officers attending that meeting, that you be able to deal with someone who was in charge of armed forces in the Srebrenica enclave, or in command?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I was not with the command of the then 2nd Corps of the ABiH but as a soldier I would suppose they had to have some sort of communication in order to regulate the situation, if possible, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if the -- there was any mention of anyone who might have been in command of ABiH army forces in Srebrenica at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: We all knew that the commander there at the time was Brigadier Naser Oric. No one asked that as a separate question or an issue. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, that would probably be an appropriate moment. I know it's five minutes early.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Doesn't make a difference, Mr. Di Fazio. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, let's continue. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, if Your Honours please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: General Delic, I'd like to show you very briefly two documents, which are headed "the Rules of Operating Procedures for the Military Security Service in the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," and secondly "The Rules of Service for the Military Police of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Could you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. please look at the two documents that are presented to you. I believe copies have been provided to the Defence. Good. Do you recognise those documents?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The English should be placed on the ELMO. The English should be placed on the ELMO although, if Your Honours please, I'm going to be extremely brief with these. I'm just seeking to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You recognise both documents. Did they apply, did these rules apply, to the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina from 1992 onwards?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are the initial rules regulating the functioning of the military police of the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, regulating in detail the work of the military security in the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. If you look at the rules relating to the military security service, they are apparently signed by the president of the Presidency and dated at 11th of September 1992, Sarajevo. That's at the back of the document. Do you -- do you find that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I found it. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And as far as you can recall or as far as you're aware, did they apply indeed from about that time, the 11th of September 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I can only speak about my immediate environment. We did our best to fully implement the rules we received.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall how long they applied for?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I believe these rules were in force throughout the war. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honour please I seek to tender that document into evidence. Namely the rules --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Shall we -- will you tender them separately as two documents or as one document? MR. DI FAZIO: I think we should tender them separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what I think as well. So let me do this. The first of these two documents that are being tendered by the Prosecution has -- starts with ERN 02131181 and ends at 02131212. MR. DI FAZIO: I think that's the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to say -- no, no, no. These are the rules of service for the military police of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Right? And this is being tendered and marked as Prosecution Exhibit P558. The other document that the Prosecution seeks to tender and which is being admitted is entitled "The Rules of Operating Procedures for the Military Security Service in the Armed Forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina," dated 1992, and in the English version starts with ERN number L0060579 and runs through and inclusive of L0060606. The Serbo-Croat version, corresponding Serbo-Croat version starts at ERN 02131159 and runs through and includes as the last page 02131180. This document is being marked Prosecution Exhibit P559. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Are you happy with that, Mr. Di Fazio? MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just on that lass document P559, in order to save time this document was signed on the 11th of September 1992, apparently created on that date, and bears the endorsement of the president of the Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic. Did it apply, as far as you're aware, from about that date, the 11th of September 1992, throughout the remainder of the war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have confirmed that. There were amendments and changes added on later in the rules of service for the military police but this is the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, do you know -- if you don't know, say so, I don't know what sort of memory you have, but would you be able to comment at all on what amendments and changes were made later? And when they were made?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I guess these were some smaller changes that were not regulated by the rules at first but then they meant to explain in detail the implementation of the rules.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to show you some more documents. I'd like to show you some documents. MR. DI FAZIO: Can Mr. Usher please provide the witness with P87, P88, P89 and I'll deal with them in sequence if Your Honours please but firstly if they can be given to the witness and I'll start off with P89. All of these documents are on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, over the last two days, you've been shown these documents.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before I ask you about the entries, the entries that are made into these particular documents, it's obviously apparent that this is a pro forma, standard form document. It's common to that -- all of the three exhibits that I've given you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead. In the meantime, you can, if you have the copy in English, you can put it on the ELMO as well, usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I just want to state for the record that these are documents that we'd objected to in terms of authenticity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for pointing that out, Mr. Jones. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Now, can you explain to the Trial Chamber the -- if you know, the background to this particular document, how it was created? And I'm not talking about the entries that were made into it but how and why this pro forma document was created.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I can remember, from 1997 until I retired in October 2000, a project was ongoing, a scientific project, including teams from both the civilian and military life. These were university professors from the University of Sarajevo and the soldiers participating in the war between 1992 and 1995. The aim of the project was to register the activities of the army of B and H starting from the beginning of the war and up until the Dayton agreements. It encompassed combat activities, commands and units of the AB and H, as well as all the other segments, for example, logistics, draft calls, and other activities conducted by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What was the ultimate purpose of this scientific project?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The purpose of the scientific project, of course from my point of view, was to register in historical terms the events that happened between 1992 and 1995, until its end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's not -- I don't think it's in dispute that occasionally war histories are created following cataclysmic events such as these. Is -- was this raw material for a war history? Or am I -- is my suggestion wrong?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I believe this was used as a starting point to learn about the real events that took place during that time concerning different aspects of activity of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And so was this a -- in effect, a standard form document that was sent to military elements or units for completion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The institution in charge of the project was the joint command of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Together with a team that worked on the project, the command drafted the form and sent them -- sent it to the corps commanders. Through the hierarchy of command and control, they forwarded such forms to their subordinate units and formations who were then in turn supposed to form teams to deal with various areas including direct participants as well as including people from various commands. Once filled out, the forms should have been forwarded to the joint command which then conducted the scientific analysis together with the team in order to have a complete picture in one place pertaining to various domains of activities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the document required to be countersigned once the information had been collated and the form filled out?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: You are correct. By hierarchy, the documents were signed by the person authorised, the person who sent it to the commands at all levels. That was also the guarantee that the documents were properly filled in and that they present a sound basis to continue with the project.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now -- Mr. Usher, would you make sure the witness has P89?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. Are you finished with this document or will you be referring to it -- MR. DI FAZIO: I've still got a lot more to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. No, no. Then I keep my mouth shut because if you had finished then obviously I had a question, but if you haven't finished I will let you put the questions. MR. DI FAZIO: I've got more questions about this series of documents, these three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of the three documents I've asked you to look in particular, I want you now to focus on P89 and go to the last page of that document. There is an entry there for "commandant to sign." Whose signature is there?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose is it? Whose signature?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: This is my signature, but only the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Put there by your hand?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, I signed this by hand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall signing such forms, and of course if you can tell us about this particular one, by all means do, but my question is first framed in the general, general terms. Did you complete such forms and -- sorry, not complete. Sign such forms once they had been completed during the life of this scientific project?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, as an authorised person and as a commander, I signed this form without going into its contents because the persons who were responsible for that filled in this form, and I, as the commander, was duty-bound to sign it. My subordinate commanders did the same. I personally participated in filling in several of these forms because as the commander of the municipal staff of the Tuzla Territorial Defence, and as the commander of the 5th Tuzla operative group, I was a direct implementer of certain combat operations and I had to provide the necessary information. And these units consulted me in order to avoid making mistakes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have the expectation that the form had been completed as honestly and as accurately as was possible in all of the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: I object to the leading nature of that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Objection sustained. MR. DI FAZIO: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you go to the font of the document, please? This document, P89, apparently deals with a description of a combat operation being an attack on a place called Bjelovac. Do you know Bjelovac at all?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No. I was never there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm going to ask you questions about the interaction and how to read this document, in particular paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4. Paragraph 1 is pretty clear, I don't need to ask you anything about that. What does paragraph 2 -- what sort of information does it contain?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, paragraph 2 says the unit that participated in the combat operation and it has all the information about that unit, about its command and other information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 3 is an entry relating to the officer who was most responsible for planning the -- the combat operation and it says it was Mr. Oric. That speaks for itself. Paragraph 4, can I ask you to look at paragraph 4? That's an entry requiring information about the "composition of the defence or liberation unit in charge of the operation during its execution." And then it gives the name of the unit and it says it was the Srebrenica TO, and that the commander was Mr. Oric. Can you explain to the Trial Chamber, in simple and clear terms, the interaction between paragraph 4 and paragraph 2? We are laymen and you're a soldier - just let me finish my question - and you can provide us insight as to how the two should be read. It would appear that the commander in charge of the combat operation is Senahid Tabakovic but that the commanding unit and its commander was Mr. Oric and the Srebrenica TO. Explain to the Trial Chamber how the two interact.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I personally have a slightly different interpretation. It's correct that in paragraph 2 it says that the unit in charge of the combat activities participating in the attack on Bjelovac was the Skenderovici Battalion. The commander of which was a Senahid Tabakovic if I'm reading this correctly. The link between paragraph 2 and paragraph 4, in my view, is that this unit which carried out these combat operations was part of the establishment of a higher unit and that was the Srebrenica Territorial Defence. That's how I interpret this, because the title of paragraph 4 says that it was in its composition.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if you can repeat the procedure of yesterday, I have the impression that this is a mistaken translation into English. That is why the Prosecutor is putting these questions. If the interpreters could see paragraph 4 in Bosnian and translate it into English, this is what the witness is actually talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Let's -- there is nothing one can lose by doing that and perhaps we can understand better. Can I ask, please, the relative interpreters to translate -- MR. DI FAZIO: On Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On Sanction, yes, paragraph -- what you have in paragraph 4. I think if you look at it it's much better than if I try to pronounce it because the general might censor me if I do not pronounce it well. It starts with [B/C/S spoken]. Can someone start translating into English?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The defence-liberating which is the bearer or exponent of combat operations during their execution was within the composition of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you happy with it Ms. Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I'm very grateful to the Defence for their clarification because it solves --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think so. MR. DI FAZIO: -- the problem I've been labouring under for the last two days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It answers your question actually. MR. DI FAZIO: It does, it does.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. You may proceed, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, we don't -- I can abandon my questions to you regarding the interaction between 2 and 4 because I now understand the interaction, and the document speaks for itself now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perhaps he can tell us while you look further into the documents whether he knows who filled this document -- who filled it in or filled it up, who wrote the insertions, in other words, and am I correct in -- yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in all the units, teams were designated for certain areas that the project was dealing with. Thus, teams for the execution of combat operations were designated. In this document, you can see who filled in and who revised the information entered into this document. You can see this on the last page of the document, which bears number 02 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where, on the left-hand side, there is the date and the place where the form was filled in, who filled in the form, and the sentence, the revisers of the information and then they list the revisers. Also on the right-hand page of the document, it says what the source of the information is. The reason is that when the war ended, we knew there would be exaggeration. We knew there would be attempts to show certain documents in a different light, and we therefore tried to reduce subjective interpretations as far as was possible. This is raw material. It had not been analysed. It was being sent to experts for analysis using scholarly and scientific methods in order to establish truth which would be relevant for us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That is precisely why I asked you the question. So I take it that this was a collective exercise by these different persons. And who chose these different persons? Who selected them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we tried to designate these persons or teams so that they would consist of people who had participated in the events and also people who had military or other expert knowledge. For example, about logistics. These were groups of three to five people dealing with these matters. I have to say here that in the case of Srebrenica itself, there were problems because when this project was being done, the unit no longer existed and some officers who had not been in Srebrenica were part of the team as well as some who had been. If this answers your question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And if we may just return to paragraphs 2 and 4, based on the information that you see in those paragraphs, can you tell the Trial Chamber who, if any person, was the overall commander of the attack on Bjelovac?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry, I do object to that question. It's a mischaracterisation of what the form itself says. As we've seen this form purports to say that Commander Senad Tabakovic was in charge of the combat operations and his unit was within the composition of the Srebrenica TO and it says Oric was the commander of the Srebrenica TO. Whereas now it's being suggested that he was the overall commander of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is what the question would be -- seeks to find out. It's precisely what the question -- MR. DI FAZIO: Any lines of subordination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. It's a perfectly legitimate question, the document being what it is and shows what it shows.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes, what the document purports to say and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's see. Let's not discuss in front of the witness. It's a perfectly legitimate question. We need to -- the witness to explain to us what all this means because we have a commander under 2, another commander or officer under 3, and then a commander under 4. What are we talking about? Who was at the top?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Might I also note that the witness said there was raw material which hadn't been analysed, essentially a draft?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: That's on the record.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyway, you know what the question is.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I remember the question, but you said Mr. Di Fazio should proceed. That's why I stopped. It is clear in paragraph 2 that these combat operations, the attack on Bjelovac [Realtime transcript read in error "Brelovac"], was being carried out by Commander Senahid Tabakovic with his battalion. He was the one who executed the task directly, who commanded the troops and executed the task directly. It's also clear, in paragraph 4, as I see it and interpret it, and I think my interpretation is correct, this battalion was part of the units of Srebrenica -- of the Srebrenica Territorial Defence, the commander of which at the time was Brigadier Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think that answers your question beautifully and in effect is a repetition of what he had stated earlier, in essence, at least. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Would Your Honours just bear with me for one moment, please? There is just a spelling mistake, line 23 should be "Bjelovac," not "Brelovac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay. That can be rectified later, Mr. Di Fazio. Let's not waste time on these things. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's go to P87. Thanks. Go back to the rear of the -- the last page of the document. There is a signature there. Do you recognise that signature? Do you know whose signature it might -- it is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Usher, please could you put it also on the ELMO for a while? MR. DI FAZIO: And it's on Sanction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And it's --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I think I'm sure that this is Mr. Hariz Saric's signature on behalf of the 28th division. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who is -- who is he, Hariz -- Hariz Saric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Hariz Saric, Brigadier, up to a few months ago, was a professional commanding officer in the command of the 2nd Corps of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina. When this report was drawn up, he was in the command of the 28th division.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And so that we can deal with this document fairly quickly, again I'd like you to look at the entries for paragraphs 1, 2, 3, 4.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in paragraph 1 of this document, it says "attack on Ducici village," "Ducice" actually, not "Ducici." It should be "Ducice." In paragraph 2 it says that "the unit which was in charge of the combat operations was the Osmace Territorial Defence," if I'm reading this right, "/Srebrenica Territorial Defence. These are two different Territorial Defences. The commander of these combat operations in the attack on Ducici was Atif Krdzic, and this paragraph contains some personal details pertaining to this command. I'm referring to Atif Krdzic. In paragraph 3 it says that the most responsible officer who was responsible for the planning of the operation was Mirsad Dudic. And then there follow the personal details of Mr. Mirsad Dudic. In paragraph 4, it says that this unit carrying out the combat operations was part of the composition of the Srebrenica TO Staff, the commander of which at the time was Brigadier Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you assist the Trial Chamber with the entry under number -- under paragraph 5 of the document? How does that -- how does the 3rd of May Brigade and the Srebrenica VT -- VTO, TO platoon, and TO Skenderovici --

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes. How does that -- how -- what participation did they have in the attack?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it states here clearly, in paragraph 5, that the defence liberation units participating jointly in this combat activity so they were cooperating, whether they were carrying out combat operations in their own areas or participating in defence or participating in some other way in the realisation of this goal, which was being carried out by the Territorial Defence of Osmace and Srebrenica. In other words, they were cooperating and this is in a strength below one battalion. In Srebrenica acting jointly with this unit, there was only one platoon numbering 30 men, the commander of which was Rajet [phoen] Memic or whatever. I can't see it very well. And this is probably a detachment, but a small one, of 180 men from Skenderovici. These are units participating, cooperating, but not involved in the action directly.
