These were not under the command of Mr. Atif Krdzic who was in charge of combat operations with these Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Territorial Defence forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And that brings me to my next question. The lines of subordination that you can discern from the interaction of paragraphs 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5, can you please explain those, that line of subordination, if any, that you can discern, to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: My response may consist of two parts. One part refers to the hierarchy in the command and control system, and the other one relates to the participation of these commands in the task itself. In my view, there is no doubt that the unit carrying out the combat operations was part of the Srebrenica TO staff, was within its composition, at least the part that participated in this action. Also, there is no doubt that the unit itself was the unit directly carrying out the task, and it was commanded by Atif Krdzic. He was the direct executor or implementer of there task. Of course in paragraph 3, we see the name of the officer who planned, who went through the thought process beforehand. I don't know Mirsad Dudic personally. He was probably part of a team from this battalion or somebody who was able to conceive the plan for this action to be carried out. May I add, Your Honours, I see here that he was a member of this unit, of this company, this Mirsad Dudic. You can see that in paragraph 3(3). He was a member of the Osmace company.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Good, thank you. MR. DI FAZIO: Can the witness now be shown P88?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, let's get through this document. Firstly, the signature at the back of the document, have you any idea whose signature that is? Don't speculate. If you don't know, say so.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No. I don't know. Someone from the 28th division but I'm not familiar with the signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, this -- on the face of it, this document appears to be the -- deal with an attack on Kravica village. And again, my -- I want you to explain any lines of subordination and command that appear to you looking at the interaction of paragraphs 1, 2, 3, 4, and 5.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, although this document has the same form, it differs in content from the document I explained previously. In paragraph 1, it says that an attack was mounted on Kravica village. In paragraph 2, it says that the unit in charge of this task was the 1st Cerani detachment, and that the immediate commander of this detachment was Semsudin Salihovic. And then there follow his personal details, ending with paragraph 2(9). In paragraph 3, it says under 3(1), that the officer most responsible for planning the combat operation, the theoretical and organisational part, that is, was Ferid Hodzic, but at the time he was the commander of the Vlasenica Territorial Defence Staff. From this, I can only conclude that the Cerani detachment was probably under the direct command of the Vlasenica TO Staff. This is the only link I can make here. In paragraph 4, it also says - and this differs from what we saw in the previous documents - that these were a joint armed forces of the subregion. So they did not belong to only one Territorial Defence Staff, Srebrenica or Vlasenica, but at least two, because it says that about 150 men participated in total, and that the commander of these joint forces -- there is something up here that I can't read, but down below I can clearly see the name of Brigadier Naser Oric. I don't know what it says above his name because the copy is bad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So from this document, do you conclude that -- that the 1st Cerani detachment and elements of the Vlasenica TO participated in this attack and that they, in turn, formed part of the joint armed forces of the subregion?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, there is no doubt that the exponent of the combat operation was the 1st Cerani detachment headed by commander Semsudin Salihovic. What is more difficult for me to say is whether there were joint armed forces of the subregion and whether there was such a commander. Although these were my units, I'm not familiar with the existence of the joint armed forces of the subregion, but that was prior to me taking over the office. From the document, one can read that the unit the 1st Cerani detachment belonged to, were called the joint armed forces of the region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Whose commander on the apparent face of the document was Naser Oric?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Under paragraph 4, when I take a look at the third column, I can't read what it says above Mr. Naser Oric's name. That is the column with the title, "Commander" and the only thing I can read here is "Naser Oric."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Thank you. I've finished with P88. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honours just give me a moment to look at my notes, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: I need to deal with some more documents, General. Can the witness be shown Exhibit P29?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've seen this document in the -- in the last two days. However, prior to coming to The Hague, were you familiar with it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. This document was created as a consequence of an agreement reached in Tuzla. The agreement was reached with Ms. Vildana Helic, the judge, regarding the attitude and actions of soldiers in respect of international humanitarian law and law of war, and I received the document and then forwarded it to my subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Very briefly, is that the signature of Knez?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the authentic signature of Mr. Zeljko Knez, at least as far as I can see. Nowadays, one can counterfeit anything, including a signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It claims at the bottom of the document that it was delivered to various TOs, and you can see they are all listed there. One of them is Srebrenica. Can you tell the Trial Chamber if you actually know whether or not this document was in fact delivered to the Srebrenica TO? And I warn you, if you don't know, say so. But if you do know anything about that issue, let us know.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, I wanted to offer some clarification prior to my answering the question. The Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina began from scratch. We used any personnel we could get to, including farmers, as well as former JNA officers, and it is clear from this document that some people did not have the educational background needed to fulfil the tasks and positions they were occupying. In the lower-left corner, it should state "to be distributed to," but not after the creation of the order. Hence, I do not wish to speculate whether these organs received the document, because prior to receiving this document we did undertake certain measures but I cannot say anything about Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the witness be shown Exhibit P319?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment while this document -- a new document is provided. In the previous document, P29, if we could see it on the ELMO again? And I need the bottom part. MR. DI FAZIO: The B/C/S version, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The B/C/S version, yes, please. I'm asking my question because although you obviously asked him the right question, namely it claims at the bottom of the document that it was delivered to the various TOs, in his answer or his first part of the answer, he says "in the lower-left corner it should state 'to be distributed to,' but not after the creation of the order." This is not exactly the same -- this is not exactly not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Distributed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because the English translation that we have for the word "[B/C/S spoken]" is distributed to or delivered to. If I read the witness properly, he is interpreting that as meaning to be distributed to but not after, not until after the creation of the order or something like that. I think he needs to clarify it. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: First of all, what is the meaning of "[B/C/S spoken]"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the clarification I offered was in order to show that this document was put together by a person who was not sufficiently experienced or trained. What it should have read was "to distribute" and not "distributed to." The first -- the latter would mean that I have already received it and "to distribute" means the competent authority should distribute this particular document to the organs specified. I said previously that the office should have the reception log as well as the log of distribution consequently. So that one could see the way the document passed through the office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But this -- but again, thank you for the explanation. It is very clear, general, but basically this confirms also that what the document actually says is that it has been delivered to. But it's obviously a mistake according to the general. It should have never shown that word. Yes, Mr. Jones.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in English, to be fair, one has to concede that one often sees documents with delivery lists and it says delivered to -- JUDGE AGIUS: Yeah, yeah, yeah. MR. JONES. It doesn't mean it has been delivered. It may be that the practice is to take off boxes as we go along. Even in English, "delivered to" doesn't mean it has been delivered. It can mean "to be delivered to." It's a shorthand, even in English I would submit. But anyway, the witness has clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. That's the important thing. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not how the witness understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: He thought it should be even clearer, that it hadn't been delivered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, if the witness can be shown P319?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise this document? Can you tell us if you've seen it before?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I saw it once the war was over, concerning some of the issues about the project that I explained previously. During the war, I did not have the opportunity to see this order that I see before me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware of the order during the war, namely the requirement, the principal requirement, that the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina shall enforce the rules of the international military law in the armed conflict?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: As a professional soldier with the former JNA and later with the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I was familiar with international humanitarian law as well as law of war. That's why in my previous answer, I mentioned that as of June, we regulated these provisions ordered by the Supreme Command or by the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, with the president who was the late Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you just keep P319 there with you but, Mr. Usher, could the witness also be shown P272? Just look at Exhibit P272, and you can see under what -- paragraph 19. Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours, in the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right. We are following it, it's okay. No, no, no, it's section 19 or it's ... MR. DI FAZIO: I misled you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: This is part of the government gazette. MR. DI FAZIO: That's right, it's not actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's -- each publication is numbered, so this is publication number 19, or decree, or rule number 19, or whatever. MR. DI FAZIO: I shouldn't have said "paragraph."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's all right. We can follow. I mean it's -- if we had a jury, it would have been a little bit different. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this gazette, Official Gazette, of the BH army, says -- contains an order, and it apparently is made pursuant to amendment L1, paragraph 5, item 3, of the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Article 9, paragraph 1, item 9 of the decree law, numbers 4/92, 6/92, 12/92. It then follows "order issued under that power," and if you look at Exhibit P319, that appears to be made under the same legislation or regulations. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. This reflects the function of the civilian bodies. Orders and decrees they made had to have been published in the Official Gazette, and it should clearly be stated as of what date they are to be put into force concerning the orders of the Supreme Command of the AB and H.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, P319 you say you didn't see until after the war but I think you said you were aware of it. What about P272, the gazette? Did you -- did you -- did you see that during the war, this particular order dealing with the requirement of compliance with international laws of war?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, when this order was put together, I was the third command in terms of hierarchy within the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. The first was the General Staff, that is the Supreme Command. Then the corps, and I was the operations group. That is the third level. And the only thing that could reach me was the excerpts from those orders as well as complete orders from my next superior command, that is the 2nd corps command. I personally saw those orders after the war. But excerpts from those orders were something I received as the commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us if the fundamentals of the order, namely the requirement of compliance with the -- with international laws of war in armed conflicts, and all of the requirements that follow thereafter, the requirement that unit commanders and individual members be responsible for the application of those laws, requirement that competent officers instigate proceedings, requirement of training and acquaintanceship and becoming acquainted with the laws of the rules of the international laws of war, forming of a commission for the international laws of war, were all of those requirements made known to members of the ABiH army after the 23rd of August 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Sorry to rise to my feet. Is that every single man in the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I was thinking along the same lines, Mr. Jones. Can you be a little bit more specific, Mr. Di Fazio? Because obviously if the question is understood as meaning each and every member of the army, how can you expect the witness to be able to answer it? MR. DI FAZIO: Very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were all of those requirements that are obviously contained here, you can read them in P319 and in P272, were measures taken to disseminate knowledge of those requirements, as far as possible, throughout the army?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, although I wanted to give you a precise answer and I want to give you a precise answer now, I cannot do that unfortunately. There are several reasons for that. It depended on the person who was commanding a given unit and its expert knowledge, knowledge of what international humanitarian law or laws of war really are, as well as the influence of that commanding personality on his soldiers and his or her ability to effectively command and control in that time of the war and under the given circumstances. I believe at least to the extent of 80 to 90 per cent I managed to implement this task. I'm personally familiar with the fact that we created a directive that we distributed down to the level of platoon, but I don't know whether we managed to reach every single environment and whether it was possible to do anything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you just give us a little more detail on how you managed to implement the task? You've already said that we created a directive that we distributed down - I assume you mean the contents of the order - down to the level of platoons?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, the witness actually said "squad."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Level of squads. And can you tell the Trial Chamber more precisely how that was accomplished, how you went about it?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: When we began with this activity at the very beginning of the war, we were in possession of an instruction by the end of May. It wasn't very detailed but it precisely defined war booty and the behaviour of a member of the armed forces, and documents exist and I believe you had one of them in your possession. Later on, as the armed forces were organised, at the level of the General Staff, a brochure was put together. I don't remember the exact title but it went something along the line the code of ethics of the members of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina or the TO. I am not sure to which one it pertained to. But we were trying to make this as close as possible to every individual soldier, combatant, because they were the people that mattered most. So we put together a small manuals and we distributed them down to the level of squad, as far as I can remember, and they usually had five to ten people. And we did that in order to see that come to life. And the manuals explained in brief the way a soldier should behave in a given situation during the war. For example, what is a war booty, what is a prisoner of war? What targets are legitimate. Some of the basics that any given soldier needed to know concerning the international humanitarian law and laws of war. If I remember correctly, there was done on the 28th or the 29th of May 1992, the District Staff also issued an order of sorts. And that was much before this particular document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: District Staff of Tuzla -- in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the district staff in Tuzla. It was in the same city and for a while we shared the same building, the Municipal and the District Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Now, you also said that later on, as the armed forces were organised, at the level of the General Staff, a brochure was put together and then you went on to describe the contents. Can you give us any idea about when that was, when this brochure was put together and distributed in the way you hoped it would occur?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I don't want to speculate, Your Honours. I believe that was in 1993 or 1994. I don't think it was in 1992. It was after 1992. The brochure does exist and you could have it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I've finished with those documents. All right. I want to ask you about military courts. Was there a military court in Tuzla in 1992?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. It was established quite soon after the aggression against Bosnia-Herzegovina began. I believe it was in June or July 1992, at the latest.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where in Tuzla was it located?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The Court in Tuzla was in the centre of the town, in the building that houses the court today. It is in the centre. I don't know the exact street names.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say it was established in June or July at the latest of 1992. Did it start to actually function, in other words deal with cases, Prosecutions and so on?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. That military court became operational right away. One can see that from the documents. They must be accessible. And the Court tried the captured enemy soldiers as well as the members of the AB and H.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there prison facilities at the -- or -- at the military court, keeping of prisoners?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: There were prison facilities in Tuzla, the centre the Tuzla. These were actually rooms in which prisoners of war were kept, as well as members of the army who had committed either breaches of discipline or crimes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber if you - only if you know, again, only if you know - if the prosecutors and the judges working there were experienced?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: These were very professional and experienced judges from the former system, and they had been in those posts for many years. There were no amateurs and no interns doing that job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You became commander of the 2nd Corps in November 1994?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Mr. Di Fazio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the Court operating throughout the second half of 1992, 1993, right up until the time you became 2nd Corps commander, and indeed, thereafter?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: The court was operating throughout the war up until the end of the imminent threat of war. I think this was in April 1996.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the time that you were commander of the 2nd Corps, did you become aware of any ABiH soldiers being charged with war crimes and dealt with in this military court in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As commander of the 2nd Corps, would you have expected to be -- to have been informed of any such cases?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I would have expected my subordinates to inform me if something like that had happened. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, my estimates of when I'm going to finish keep varying wildly. I certainly -- obviously, I'm going to comply with your requirement that we finish today, there is no question about that, but I wonder if you'd be grant -- minded to grant me the indulgence of a ten-minute early break? I think that if we do that, I can have a think about what remains, ensure that it's dealt with in the last 45 minutes, and cut out anything that's unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Mr. Di Fazio. I suppose there is no objection from your side. We'll have a 25-minute break starting from now. We'll reconvene exactly at 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Di Fazio. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you, Your Honours. It was worthwhile. I've performed some surgery on my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have already mentioned, General, that from -- you assumed command of 2nd Corps in November 1994.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to ask you about the state of communications, if any, between your 2nd Corps command headquarters and Srebrenica. Can you tell us if communications existed; if they did, what was the method of communication?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: In that period, communications with all subordinate units was set up and they were functioning within the 2nd Corps of the Army of BiH.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And was the -- were the ABiH forces operating in the Srebrenica enclave subordinate units? Subordinate to the 2nd Corps, of course.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes. They were subordinate to the 2nd Corps and they were in the area of responsibility of the 2nd Corps. You must bear in mind that Srebrenica itself was a protected and demilitarised zone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course. What was the method of communication with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Mr. Di Fazio, with Srebrenica we had a Paket radio communication. That's something similar to a teleprinter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you -- I think earlier you said that you took up your command position on the 11th of November 1994? Was it the 11th of November 1994?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No. Officially, the handover of duty was on the 19th of November 1994, although the order on my appointment as corps commander arrived on the 22nd of September of the same year, two months prior to my taking over my duty.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. All right. When you in fact took over your duties in -- on the 19th of November 1994, is that when you ascertained that the Paket radio communication was the method of communication with Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you took over the command, was this method of communication already in existence or was it something that you set up upon your taking Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. over command?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: This method of communication was already in existence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what I'd like to know, if you can tell us, can you tell us about how long before you took up your command position on the 19th of November 1994, was that Paket communication system operating? And again, you know, of course not to speculate.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. The chiefs of communications who were in the command of the 2nd Corps should know that, and there are probably documents about this. MR. DI FAZIO: Would Your Honour just give me a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any problems with the system, or did it function from the time you assumed command? With Srebrenica, I mean.

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: During the time that I communicated with Srebrenica, there were no major problems in establishing communication between Srebrenica and Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please I would like to move now to another topic and I'd like to produce a document to the witness but I think we should go into closed or private session for that purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By all means, Mr. Di Fazio. Let's go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think it's in dispute that you met Mr. Oric in 1995, shortly before the fall of Srebrenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I said so in my previous answers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't want to go into the details of all of your encounters with him. Suffice it to ask you this: Did you and he see each other from time to time for a period of about a month or so following his arrival in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes, almost on a daily basis. Or at least every second or third day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time, were you his superior officer?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During that period of time that you had contact with him in Tuzla, did he ever report to you any episodes of war crimes or criminal offences, indeed criminal offences of any nature whatsoever having been committed by soldiers under his command?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No. He never did so and we never discussed such matters.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Have you ever actually been to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you have any direct knowledge of any relationships that might have existed between individuals, the police, military police, the army, Crisis Staffs, War Presidencies, in Srebrenica in the period of time from April of 1992 until you saw Mr. Oric -- or, sorry, I'll withdraw that, until November of 1994?

utterances.speaker: SEAD DELIC
utterances.text: If I were to say anything, everything would be speculation or hear say. I can tell you I know less than any regular citizen because I didn't have much opportunity to listen to the TV or radio. Hence, I believe it to be my answer. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you very much for your answering my questions, General Delic. If Your Honours please, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Di Fazio. I would imagine -- do you want to start now, Mr. Jones?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: May I ask one question for two reasons? One so that my cross-examination is officially underway and secondly just to clarify a matter which might be nicer for all of us if it is clarified before the weekend. But I'd like to go back to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go to private session. This is in the presence of the witness, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. JONES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. So I thank you, Mr. Jones. Mr. Jones will be cross-examining you on Monday, General. In the meantime, take the opportunity of the weekend and the nice weather that we are going to have and try to relax, and we'll reconvene Monday. I think we are sitting in the morning, if I remember well. We are sitting in the morning. So you should be -- your testimony should be over by midday. Before you leave the courtroom, although you are a professional man, I would like to remind you of your responsibility not to communicate with anyone in relation to the matters that you are testifying upon. Doesn't mean to say that you cannot speak to your family, for example, or to friends or whatever, but you're not to discuss and you're not to allow anyone to approach you on matters related to your testimony. Thank you. Have a nice weekend. Yes, I recognise Mr. Wubben.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't realise. I thought you were in a hurry to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Not so quick, please. I have respect for this Honourable Bench but, Your Honours, I would like to inform you that we would like to circulate with a view to the witness on Tuesday, a declaration as a courtesy copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I thank you. You're circulating it now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WUBBEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think -- can the witness leave the courtroom? Yes, usher, please accompany the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Any further business? None? So have a nice weekend and we'll meet again, please God, on Monday. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: be reconvened on Monday, the 30th day of May, 2005, at 9.00 a.m. 23 24 25
